propositions: docs/releasing.md incorrectly describes the pypi environment's required-reviewers rule as 'the second human approval' when it is actually controlled by a single configured release identity (JoeOakhartNava) with self-review permitted and admin bypass available
docs/releasing.md and .github/workflows/release.yml claim the approval is an interactive human prompt when in fact it is routinely executed non-interactively via the pending-deployments REST API
the environment rule provides identity control over who can release the publish job, not independent code review—the actual review property comes from releasing only from Gerrit-reviewed main

the runbook must document the correct non-interactive approval mechanism: GET pending_deployments to discover environment id, then POST with an explicit JSON body typing environment_ids as an integer array, not a string flag
the rewrite must clarify what the gate guarantees (only listed reviewers can approve that specific run) and what it does not guarantee (second-party review, interactive checkpoint)
existing guards in release_guards.py validate the required-reviewers rule and main-only branch policy remain in place, so the rewrite is documentation-only with no behavioral change
